questions.prompt: In a client-server network, the central server provides the services and manages the traffic.
Which one describes a peer-to-peer network?
options: There's no central server, and each host is responsible for sharing its own resources and data
Every host connects to a central switch
One central machine stores every file and checks every login
Only two computers can ever be connected

questions.prompt: Peer-to-peer networks don't grow well past a small group. The reading's two-word summary of this drawback: "size ______". (one word)
A company's file server crashes. What happens on a client-server network?
options: Only the server's own user is affected
Nothing, the clients share the files among themselves
Every client loses access to that service, because the server is a single point of failure

questions.prompt: "Server" names a special kind of hardware. An ordinary laptop can't be a server.
Five friends at home share one printer and swap files directly between their laptops, with no dedicated server. What kind of network is this?
Which is an advantage of client-server over peer-to-peer?
options: It has no single point of failure
Security and backups are managed in one central place
It costs less to set up

questions.prompt: A file-sharing app uses a central server only to help peers find each other, then sends the files directly between peers. What's the word for a design that mixes both models? (one word)
